rows.season: Gu (main rainy season, Apr–Jun) or under irrigation year-round
rows.planting_method: Direct-seed in rows 75cm apart, 25cm between plants, 3–5cm deep. Plant 2 seeds per hole and thin to the strongest seedling after 2 weeks. Prepare land by ploughing to 20–25cm depth and breaking clods before sowing.
rows.irrigation: Needs 500–800mm of water over the growing cycle. Under irrigation, water every 7–10 days; increase frequency during tasseling and grain-filling (the most water-sensitive stages). Avoid waterlogging — ensure furrows drain freely.
rows.fertilizer: Apply well-rotted manure or compost at land preparation (10–15 tons/ha). Basal dose: DAP or NPK 20-20-0 at planting. Top-dress with urea at knee-height (30 days) and again at tasseling for stronger grain fill.
rows.common_pests: Fall armyworm, stem borer, maize streak virus

rows.planting_method: Drill seed in rows 20cm apart at 3–4cm depth, seed rate ~120kg/ha. Fine, level seedbed is essential for even germination and irrigation flow.
rows.irrigation: Requires 450–650mm total. Critical irrigation stages: crown root initiation (~21 days), tillering, flowering, and grain-filling. Light, frequent irrigation is better than flooding.
rows.fertilizer: Apply full phosphorus and half nitrogen at sowing. Top-dress remaining nitrogen (urea) split between tillering and heading stages for best grain protein and yield.

rows.season: Transplant during cooler months; irrigated year-round
rows.planting_method: Raise seedlings in a nursery bed for 6–8 weeks, then transplant at 10–15cm spacing in rows 20cm apart once seedlings reach pencil thickness. Raised beds improve drainage and bulb quality.
rows.irrigation: Shallow-rooted crop needing frequent light irrigation every 3–5 days, especially during bulb formation. Reduce and eventually stop watering 2–3 weeks before harvest to allow the neck to dry down.
rows.fertilizer: Incorporate compost/manure before transplanting. Apply nitrogen and potassium in split doses — heavier early for leaf growth, tapering off once bulbing begins to avoid soft bulbs and poor storage life.

rows.season: Best planted at the start of the dry season under irrigation
rows.planting_method: Start seedlings in a nursery for 3–4 weeks, transplant when 4–5 true leaves appear. Space plants 45–60cm apart in rows 90–100cm apart to allow airflow. Stake or trellis to keep fruit off the soil.
rows.irrigation: Consistent moisture is critical — irrigate every 4–7 days, more often in sandy soil. Uneven watering causes blossom-end rot and fruit cracking, so keep soil moisture steady rather than wet-then-dry.
rows.fertilizer: Apply compost and a phosphorus-rich basal fertilizer at transplanting to build strong roots. Side-dress with balanced NPK at flowering and again at first fruit set; avoid excess nitrogen, which produces leafy plants with poor fruiting.
rows.common_pests: Whitefly, tuta absoluta (leaf miner moth), blight
